AfterObtained.rationale: STALE (round 11 re-settle): this rollup summarised guards G1 (RNG-stream burn) and N1 (the other-character card pool). G1 was closed 2026-07-29 round 6 and the guard entry itself already reads `faithful` -- the hooks-level entry was simply never revisited. EXECUTED (source read, sts2_rl/relics/sea_glass.py:31-38): `after_obtained` burns `self.CARDS` (15) `run.player_rng.rewards.next_int(2)` draws in a parity run and is a documented no-op only in legacy RL play (no Rewards stream to desync). N1 remains a `waiver`, not a gap -- the CARDS themselves are genuinely out of scope (the shared contract names 'other characters' explicitly, and Orobas.cs:190/204 guarantees the assigned CharacterId is never the player's own), so a single-character sim has nothing to draw from; the RNG-stream half that IS in scope is the half G1 already fixed. Same convention as this record's own N4 (undo_after_obtained, vacuous here) and the sibling pattern in relic/fiddle's ShouldDraw entry (a hook reaching `faithful` over a residual out-of-scope waiver). Nothing gap-classified remains under this hook.

guards.what: G1: the 15 CardFactory.CreateForReward draws on PlayerRng.Rewards are never consumed, so every later Rewards draw in the run is shifted
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): the 15 Rewards draws are consumed. SeaGlass.cs:85-87 calls CardFactory.CreateForReward three times with `Cards.IntValue / 3` == 5, and each card costs exactly ONE `PlayerRng.Rewards.NextItem` (CardFactory.cs:235-236) with no upgrade roll -- ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds sets NoUpgradeRoll (CardCreationOptions.cs:162) and SeaGlass's WithFlags ORs onto it (:212-216), which is why the count is 15 and not 30. relics/sea_glass.py now burns them in a parity run. The entry's own caveat -- that a faithful fix seemed to need the other character's pool -- turned out not to apply to the STREAM half: Rng.next_int costs one MegaRandom draw whatever its range (rng.py:178-180), so the counter lands where the game's does without knowing which cards were named. The CARDS remain out of scope and are documented as such in the port, not re-verdicted here. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py sea-glass` reports the Rewards counter 0 -> 15 where it reported 0 -> 0.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: SeaGlass.cs:81 computes `cardCount = base.DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue / 3` == 15 / 3 == 5 (CardsVar(15), SeaGlass.cs:70, no AscensionHelper branch in the file), and lines 85-87 call CardFactory.CreateForReward three times with 5 cards each. CreateForReward draws each card off `options.RngOverride ?? player.PlayerRng.Rewards` (CardFactory.cs:98-101 for the upgrade roll, and the per-card pick inside CreateForReward), and Sea Glass passes no RngOverride -- so 15 reward-stream draws happen whether the player keeps any card or not. The sim's stub consumes nothing. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py sea-glass): with a parity rng_set attached, `add_relic('sea_glass')` moves the player Rewards counter 0 -> 0 and the deck 10 -> 10. LIVE for RNG parity -- Sea Glass is reachable on any seed whose Orobas roll lands above 1/3, and every subsequent Rewards consumer (combat card rewards, the treasure chest's gold, relic rarity rolls, Scroll Boxes' own bundles) then reads at the wrong stream position -- and DORMANT for RL play. Same live/dormant split and same shape as relic/calling_bell G2 (unconsumed PullNextRelicFromFront draws) and relic/astrolabe N1 (an unpassed named stream); recorded as a gap, not a waiver, because stream position is in scope even though the CARDS are not. Note the fix is awkward and should be scoped deliberately: reproducing the draw count faithfully requires the other character's pool, which the sim does not have, so a parity fix here means either porting the pools or burning the right number of draws against a placeholder. Rule 7: CardFactory.cs, events/orobas.py and rng.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: the effect itself -- 5 Common / 5 Uncommon / 5 Rare cards from ANOTHER character's CardPool, offered as a grid pick (SeaGlass.cs:82-92)
guards.rationale: Genuinely out of scope under the shared contract's rule 1, which names 'other characters' explicitly, and the scope is not incidental -- it is the relic's whole design. Established by reading the ASSIGNMENT path rather than assumed from the relic: Orobas.cs:190 picks `base.Rng.NextItem(Owner.UnlockState.Characters.Where(c => c.Id != character.Id))` and line 204 stamps that id onto the relic, and Orobas.cs:44-53's SeaGlassOptions builds one option per character in ModelDb.AllCharacters. So the CharacterId is always a character other than the player's, and the sim -- which has exactly one character's card pool -- has nothing to draw from. The sim's own docstring (sea_glass.py:8-12) states this correctly, which is worth recording against PROMPT.md class 12: this is the rare stub whose premise checks out. The one arm that would be in scope is unreachable in the shipping game: SeaGlass.cs:76-80 defaults CharacterId to Ironclad, but only after `Log.Error("Sea Glass was obtained without a character ID assigned! This could be a bug, or the player could have used the console")` -- an error path, not behaviour. Rule 7: Orobas.cs, events/orobas.py and Log.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: no state to reset and no other C# override -- PROMPT.md classes 10 and 13 checked
guards.rationale: SeaGlass.cs's only field is `_characterId`, set once at grant time and read only by Title/Character; there is no combat or turn hook to lose a reset. Read both files. Note this relic is NOT in sweep A's candidate list precisely because the sim port holds no fields at all.

Vacuous at this site and recorded to say so explicitly: the stub mutates no run state, so there is nothing for an undo to reverse and the conformance-runner consequence the other units in this batch carry does not arise here. Per PROMPT.md v6 binding item 3, the ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is faithful at every site: the helper has no C# counterpart -- nothing in the game un-picks a relic -- so a sim lacking it is not diverging from the source, which is the only question this audit asks. Flagged for its operational consequence only, which is a tooling defect and not a fidelity gap. Rule 7: relics/base.py:143-150 and conformance/runner.py are not hashed here.
